newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's KPB palmoil agency may see shake-up.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's KPB palmoil agency may see shake-up.

text.p: The suspension of crude palm oil exports by Indonesia's state-run joint marketing agency (KPB) could signal the start of a shake-up under its new leadership, industry sources said on Thursday.
"There are likely to be other changes in the pipeline," an agriculture ministry source told Reuters.
"I expect personnel changes," said the official, who has previous experience in working with the KPB.
The agency has suspended signing of new crude palm oil export contracts in October in a bid to clear a backlog of previous commitments, a KPB official said on Wednesday.
The suspension comes after the appointment of Zaini Taibin as KPB boss last month.
Traders said the export halt, which drove up prices on the Malaysian and European markets on Wednesday, was due to overselling in previous months.
They said there was market talk that Taibin ordered the suspension as part of his house-cleaning but added that there was a possibility that exports could resume later this month.
"I don't think it (suspension) will be allowed to go into November," one senior trader said. "There's a chance exports will resume later this month."
The KPB markets all crude palm oil produced by state plantations, of which 30 percent is exported and the rest channelled into the local market.
State plantations account for nearly 40 percent of total national production, which was about 4.5 million tonnes last year and are forecast to rise to 4.9 million in 1996.
Traders said foreign-registered companies planning to buy crude palm oil from the KPB have to register with an Indonesian company, Indoham, based in Hamburg.
"Indoham then sends the list of interested buyers to the KPB, which picks those who will get the oil," one trader said.

He said there were also local firms which had set up operations overseas so that they can apply to buy Indonesian oil. "This way they can sell in Europe without paying an export tax, which local (Indonesian) exporters have to," he said.
